standard.title: Music across cultures and contexts
standard.description: explore where, why and how people across cultures, communities and/or other contexts experience music
standard.prior_knowledge: Students have explored how arts are important for people and communities (AC9AMUFE01) and can identify arts works in their own life. They have not yet formally explored music across diverse cultural or community contexts, or considered the different roles people play in relation to music.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students explore where, why and how people across cultures, communities and other contexts experience music, and share observations about music preferences and purposes.

nodes.label: Where and how people experience music
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify multiple places and ways people experience music — including as performer, composer and audience.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify at least two different contexts in which people experience music (e.g. at home, at a concert, in a game, in a ceremony).
nodes.typical_width: Explore the full range of contexts in which people experience music — at home, in performance spaces, in public spaces, via streaming, in games and screen-based products, in ceremonies; identify different roles (singer, songwriter, composer, instrumentalist, sound engineer, digital producer, audience member).
wider: Map the places and roles of musicians in the school and local community — create a class list of who the musicians are and what they do
Investigate how music is used in screen-based products (games, cartoons, e-books) — ask 'How is the music telling me what to feel?' and 'Who made this music?'

response_modes.reason: Students' awareness of music contexts is limited to their personal experience at Y1-2. Broadening the contexts they are aware of (ceremonial, digital, community, screen-based) builds the foundation for understanding why music is created for specific purposes and audiences.

success_criteria: Can name at least two different contexts in which people experience music
Can identify at least one role a person plays in relation to music (beyond audience)

nodes.label: Music from diverse cultures
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can listen to music from at least one culture or community different from their own and share observations about instruments, voices and purpose.
nodes.minimum_width: Listen to music from one culturally diverse context; identify at least one instrument or voice used and describe one feature of the music.
nodes.typical_width: Listen to music from multiple culturally diverse contexts; identify instruments and voices; describe the purpose the music was composed for (e.g. dance, ceremony, celebration, storytelling); share personal responses to the music.
wider: Compare two pieces from different cultural contexts created for similar purposes (e.g. two different celebration songs) — what is similar and what is different?
Explore music from a cultural group represented in the class or local community — share what community members know about the music's purpose and context

response_modes.reason: The range of cultural music contexts encountered at Y1-2 determines the breadth of students' understanding of why and how people make music. Each new cultural context adds evidence for the diversity of musical purpose and practice.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Music from diverse cultural contexts at Y1-2 builds curiosity and openness that is difficult to develop later. The First Nations elaborations in AC9AMU2E02 extend this further — this node provides the listening and observation skills that make that work accessible.
success_criteria: Listens to music from at least one unfamiliar cultural context
Can identify at least one instrument or voice and describe one feature of the music (e.g. 'it uses a drum and sounds fast')

nodes.label: Personal music preferences and experiences
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can discuss their own music preferences and compare them with peers and family members, linking preferences to where and how music is experienced.
nodes.minimum_width: Share one music preference (a type of music, a song, or a context they like music in) and give a reason.
nodes.typical_width: Discuss music preferences with peers and family; identify what music they encounter daily and in what contexts; compile or imagine a playlist that combines favourites from different people or generations; practise active listening (moving with the beat, clapping rhythmic ideas).
wider: Compile a family or community playlist combining music from different generations — discuss what each piece means to the people who love it
Investigate how music preferences relate to cultural identity — interview a family member about music important to them and share findings with the class

response_modes.reason: This node integrates context awareness with personal response — students connect what they know about how music works in different contexts to their own experience of music. The teaching investment is in making the connection between 'music happens in many contexts' and 'I encounter music in specific contexts for specific reasons.'

success_criteria: Can share a music preference and give at least one reason
Can connect their preference to a context in which they experience that music (e.g. 'I listen to it at home', 'my family plays it at celebrations')
